Zoom determines retention periods based on legal position regarding agreement enforcement, dispute resolution, and statutes of limitations.
Users in EEA, Switzerland, or UK have the right to access personal data held about them.
Users in EEA, Switzerland, or UK have the right to receive their personal data for portability to another provider.
Users in EEA, Switzerland, or UK have the right to erasure of personal data in certain circumstances.
Users in EEA, Switzerland, or UK have the right to object to processing of their personal data.
Users in EEA, Switzerland, or UK have the right to stop receiving marketing communications.
Users in EEA, Switzerland, or UK have the right to require correction of inaccurate or incomplete personal data.
Users in EEA, Switzerland, or UK have the right to restrict processing of their personal data in certain circumstances.

Users have the right to lodge a complaint with a data protection authority regarding our data practices.
Zoom transfers, stores, and processes personal data globally outside the country where it was initially collected.
Personal data may be transferred to the United States and other countries outside the EEA, Switzerland, and UK.
Zoom protects personal data in accordance with its Privacy Statement wherever it is processed.
Zoom uses European Commission standard contractual clauses to govern transfers to countries without adequate data protection.
Zoom complies with the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, UK Extension, and Swiss-U.S. Data Privacy Framework.

Zoom has certified adherence to Swiss-U.S. DPF Principles for processing personal data from Switzerland.
DPF Principles govern in case of conflict with Zoom's privacy policy terms.

Zoom remains liable if third-party agents process personal data inconsistently with DPF Principles.
